extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of political philosophy; lawmakers and legislators interested in principles of lawcraft and constitutions
extracted.subtask_description: Guiding principles for framing and evaluating laws, constitutions, and civic institutions in a polis — covering property distribution, family and military organisation, magistracy selection, judicial procedure, amendment of laws, and population policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid making wives and property entirely common
rubrics_metrics.description: It is also very hazardous to settle the magistracy as Socrates has done; for he would have persons of the same rank always in office... Besides, it is of no little consequence, nor is it easy to determine, how these should be framed so as to preserve the community of the military.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commonality of wives without clear arrangements for domestic management undermines care of household affairs. Making property common as well does not remedy inconvenience. Drawing analogies from brute animals (i.e. to justify communal marriage/property) is absurd because human family associations differ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid a permanent magistracy of the same rank
rubrics_metrics.description: It is also very hazardous to settle the magistracy as Socrates has done; for he would have persons of the same rank always in office, which becomes the cause of sedition...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perpetual occupation of office by the same rank breeds sedition, especially among courageous or warlike citizens; the legislator must consider how offices are filled to avoid entrenched elites and unrest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim at the happiness of every individual citizen
rubrics_metrics.description: the legislator ought to make all the citizens happy; but it is impossible that the whole city can be happy, without all, or the greater, or some part of it be happy. For happiness... must exist in every individual
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Happiness is not additive across parts of a city; laws should secure individual well-being (particularly of pivotal groups like the military) because if essential groups are unhappy the whole city cannot be considered happy.

rubrics_metrics.name: When framing laws consider both the country and the people
rubrics_metrics.description: a legislator should have two things in view when he frames his laws, the country and the people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laws must be adapted to geographic, economic, and demographic realities as well as to the character and customs of the population; what works in one country/people may not in another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take neighbouring states and external relations into account
rubrics_metrics.description: He will also do well, if he has some regard to the neighbouring states, if he intends that his community should maintain any political intercourse with them...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citizens should be trained in warfare suited not only to their own terrain but to enemies they may encounter; foreign policy and defence considerations must shape domestic law and military organisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fix property allotments and regulate population growth together
rubrics_metrics.description: It may also be considered whether the quantity of each person's property may not be settled in a different manner... It is more necessary than even to regulate property, to take care that the increase of the people should not exceed a certain number; and in determining that, to take into consideration those children who will die, and also those women who will be barren
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Property distribution schemes require demographic planning; failure to coordinate land/wealth allotments with fertility and mortality risks poverty and collapse of property rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prescribe both moderate and liberal standards of living
rubrics_metrics.description: a man may live moderately and miserably at the same time; he had therefore better have proposed, that they should live both moderately and liberally
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulation of subsistence should aim at sufficiency without inducing wretchedness or fostering luxury; laws about wealth should consider virtues like prudence and liberality rather than mere subsistence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide determinate property division that accounts for population change
rubrics_metrics.description: It is also absurd to render property equal, and not to provide for the increasing number of the citizens; but to leave that circumstance uncertain...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Property-equality schemes must specify how allotments change as the citizen population grows; laissez-faire assumptions about natural regulation are inadequate in tightly structured polities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish clearly between governors and the governed
rubrics_metrics.description: He has also neglected in that treatise to point out how the governors are to be distinguished from the governed; for he says, that as of one sort of wool the warp ought to be made, and of another the woof, so ought some to govern, and others to be governed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The legislator must define the institutional, property, and functional boundaries between rulers and ruled (including whether property increases apply equally), otherwise roles and legitimacy are unclear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid impractical housing or resource allotments
rubrics_metrics.description: he appoints two houses to each person, separate from each other; but it is inconvenient for a person to inhabit two houses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design material allocations (housing, allotments) to be practically usable and not merely theoretical; impractical prescriptions breed disorder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blend elements of multiple government forms for stability
rubrics_metrics.description: Some persons say, that the most perfect government should be composed of all others blended together... those propose what is much better who blend many governments together; for the most perfect is that which is formed of many parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A mixed constitution combining monarchy, oligarchy, and democracy can balance competing interests; the precise blend must be chosen to suit the polity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design electoral mechanisms to avoid favoring the wealthy
rubrics_metrics.description: to choose them by lot is common to both; but that a man of fortune must necessarily be a member of the assembly... makes the state incline to an oligarchy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Election rules (lot, vote compulsion, class obligations) can inadvertently concentrate power among the wealthy; avoid structures that reduce participation or compel unequal burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent self-perpetuating selection of governing bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: There will also great danger arise from the manner of electing the senate, when those who are elected themselves are afterwards to elect others; for by this means, if a certain number choose to combine together... the election will always fall according to their pleasure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid selection processes where an elected group selects successors without wider checks, since small coalitions can capture power and entrench themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulate private property because neglect breeds sedition
rubrics_metrics.description: There are some persons who think, that the first object of government should be to regulate well everything relating to private property; for they say, that a neglect herein is the source of all seditions whatsoever.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Property law (limits, inheritance, restrictions on sale) is foundational to domestic peace; legislators should prioritize stable property regimes to reduce conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate equality-of-wealth proposals with family and education policy
rubrics_metrics.description: That an equality of goods was in some degree serviceable to strengthen the bands of society... But he should have said particularly what education he intended... for this education may be one, and yet such as will make the citizens over-greedy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material equality alone is insufficient; it must be paired with education and cultural formation, otherwise equal wealth may lead to ambition for honors or other disruptive desires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer similarity of sentiments via education over mere material equality
rubrics_metrics.description: it is of more consequence that the citizen should entertain a similarity of sentiments than an equality of circumstances; but this can never be attained unless they are properly educated under the direction of the law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laws should include educational and civic institutions that cultivate shared values; cohesion depends more on shared character than identical fortunes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address the three causes of theft with targeted remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: To prevent stealing from necessity, let every one be supplied with a moderate subsistence... to prevent stealing to procure the luxuries of life, temperance be enjoined; and thirdly, let those who wish for pleasure in it itself seek for it only in philosophy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different motives for crime require different policy tools: subsistence provision, moral education or legal penalties for luxury-driven crime, and civic/philosophical cultivation to redirect desires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set wealth levels to avoid inviting invasion yet enable defence
rubrics_metrics.description: it should not be so much as to tempt those who are near, and more powerful to invade it, any more than he would those who had not so much as yourself; thus when Autophradatus proposed to besiege Atarneus, Eubulus advised him to consider what time it would require to take the city
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Economic and material prosperity should be balanced against strategic vulnerability: avoid making the state a tempting target or so poor it cannot defend itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely solely on material equality to suppress ambition
rubrics_metrics.description: There is, indeed, some advantage in an equality of goods amongst the citizens to prevent seditions; and yet, to say truth, no very great one... it is the nature of our desires to be boundless
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material equalization can curb petty crimes but cannot eliminate ambition-driven political disorder; other institutional and moral measures are needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply property regulation to all forms of wealth, not just land
rubrics_metrics.description: Nor has he treated well the equality of goods, for he has extended his regulation only to land; whereas a man's substance consists not only in this, but also in slaves, cattle, money, and all that variety of things which fall under the name of chattels
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If legislating equality or limits, include slaves, livestock, money, and other chattels, or else specify rules for those categories to avoid loopholes and inequities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage public artisans and non-citizen labor to avoid creating hostile classes
rubrics_metrics.description: it appears too by his laws, that he intends to establish only a small state, as all the artificers are to belong to the public... if all those who are to be employed in public works are to be the slaves of the public... there will be a fourth order in the state which will have no share in it, and always entertain hostile sentiments towards it
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutionalising large non-citizen or slave labor classes without civic inclusion risks alienation and possible conflict; the labour structure must be designed to preserve social cohesion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide appellate courts for causes thought unjustly decided
rubrics_metrics.description: He ordered also that there should be a particular court of appeal, into which all causes might be removed which were supposed to have been unjustly determined elsewhere; which court should be composed of old men chosen for that purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An appeals mechanism staffed by experienced judges can correct injustices; composition and selection of such bodies require careful design to prevent bias or capture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use clear judicial verdict forms to avoid perjury and confusion
rubrics_metrics.description: He thought also that they should not pass sentence by votes; but that every one should bring with him a tablet, on which he should write, that he found the party guilty... he disapproved of that general custom already established, as it obliges the judges to be guilty of perjury if they determined positively either on the one side or the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judicial procedures should allow judges to express nuanced verdicts without forcing absolute binary positions that could constitute perjury. Conversely, Aristotle criticises the tablet-splitting/arbitration idea for producing inconsistent penalties among judges—so verdict forms must be both honest and practical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid rewarding informers in ways that encourage commotion
rubrics_metrics.description: with respect to these honours which he proposes to bestow on those who can give any information useful to the community... it would encourage informers, and probably occasion commotions in the state
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incentives for whistleblowing or reform must be designed so they do not turn into bounty-hunting that destabilises public order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make law amendment possible but safeguard against trivial or frequent change
rubrics_metrics.description: Nor is it, moreover, right to permit written laws always to remain without alteration... But if we consider this matter in another point of view, it will appear to require great caution; for when the advantage proposed is trifling, as the accustoming the people easily to abolish their laws is of bad consequence, it is evidently better to pass over some faults
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laws should be amendable to address particulars and evolving needs, but frequent or easy amendment weakens legal authority; balance flexibility with the stabilizing force of custom and written rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid rigid social divisions that concentrate power in one class
rubrics_metrics.description: The artisans, the husbandmen, and the soldiers are to compose one community, where the husbandmen are to have no arms, and the artisans neither arms nor land, which would in a manner render them slaves to the soldiery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Occupational or class divisions that deny arms, land, or political share to some orders tend to make them subservient and to alienate them from the commonwealth; inclusion and fair share in governance are important for loyalty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocate land explicitly for sacred, public (military), and private uses
rubrics_metrics.description: he also divided the lands into three parts, and allotted one to sacred purposes, another to the public, and the third to individuals. The first of these was to supply what was necessary for the established worship of the gods; the second was to be allotted to the support of the soldiery; and the third was to be the property of the husbandman.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Land policy should deliberately provide for religious needs, public support (notably military), and private agriculture so that state functions and cultic obligations are sustainable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose high magistrates by law/custom and qualifications, not accidentally
rubrics_metrics.description: This magistracy is indeed the great support of the state; but as it is quite accidental what sort of persons they may be, it is not right that they should determine according to their own opinion, but by a written law or established custom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Magistracies that exercise great power (e.g., ephori) must be filled from a qualified pool and constrained by law/custom to reduce susceptibility to bribery and arbitrary acts; selection by chance or without qualification risks corruption and tyranny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulate women's freedoms and property to maintain civic order
rubrics_metrics.description: As to the indulging of women in any particular liberties, it is hurtful to the end of government and the prosperity of the city... when the manners of the women are not well regulated... it must not only occasion faults which are disgraceful to the state, but also increase the love of money.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excessive female autonomy (in that society's terms) may destabilise civic norms and priorities; inheritance and marriage laws affecting women's property should be calibrated to maintain sufficient male citizen numbers and civic responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design population incentives mindful of land division consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: to make them desirous of having large families he ordered that he who had three children should be excused the night-watch, and that he who had four should pay no taxes: though it is very evident, that while the land was divided in this manner, that if the people increased there must many of them be very poor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Population encouragement measures (tax relief, exemptions) must be consistent with available land and wealth; otherwise incentives can increase numbers while producing widespread poverty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure magistrates' mode of life fits civic virtues and law
rubrics_metrics.description: Their way of life also is not consistent with the manners of the city, for it is too indulgent; whereas that of others is too severe; so that they cannot support it, but are obliged privately to act contrary to law, that they may enjoy some of the pleasures of sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Officials whose private conduct deviates from civic norms undermine respect for law; selection, oversight, and institutional constraints should align magistrates' incentives with public virtue.
